newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLOs room for more gains hangs on U.S. payrolls.
newsitem.headline: OLOs room for more gains hangs on U.S. payrolls.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds (OLOs) ended at the day highs on Thursday as the market was lifted by a strong performance in neighbouring Germany.

But OLO dealers said the market had little room to climb higher until Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls data were out of the way. August payrolls, due for release at 1230 GMT, are seen up around 245,000 with unemployment falling to around 5.3 from 5.4 percent in July. Average earnings are seen up 0.2 percent.
A strong number would raise fears the U.S. Federal Reserve would hike rates at its next policy meeting on September 24. A weaker number might see the move postponed until November.
The yield on benchmark 10-year OLOs ended at around 6.62 percent with the spread over Bunds at 25 basis points, up one from Wednesday.
Dealers said the curve flattened slightly as the long end gained more than shorter maturities, in line with a similar move in Germany. "The short end is very expensive," one dealer said.
Front month OLO futures, which expire on September 25, ended up 0.18 at 116.62, just off their high of 116.67 but well up from their low at 116.40.
